data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The smallest positive integer satisfying x\u22613 (mod 5) and x\u22614 (mod 7) is 18.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the arithmetic progression 3+5k is interrupted by a prime-modulus wormhole such that 3+5k jumps directly to 23 for k=3, the enumeration would miss 18.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the identity of remainder operations is falsified and division by 7 operates under a non-Euclidean modulus where remainder 4 is equivalent to remainder -3, x=4 might be reported as the minimal solution.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Anchor in bounded empirical enumeration of the progression 3, 8, 13, 18, ... for the x\u22613 (mod 5) condition, and test each for the x\u22614 (mod 7) condition. The values to test are 3, 8, 13, and 18. Checking x mod 7 for these gives 3, 1, 6, and 4. Since 18 leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 5 and 4 when divided by 7, and no smaller positive integer in the sequence does, 18 is the minimal positive solution.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
